findings.where: "Good for" section: all twelve tags (First-time surfers, Remote workers, Long stays, Meeting people, Yoga, Nightlife, Budget, Cafés, Couples, Solo travellers, Scooter riders, Sunsets), at both widths
findings.fault: The tags do nothing when tapped, but they look like buttons or filters. Each one is a filled pill with a 2 px coloured border, in a mix of saturated colours. That is how a selectable filter chip looks, and on a hostel site it reads as "show me hostels for solo travellers". The colours also change from tag to tag for no reason, which suggests they sort the tags into kinds when they don't. When nothing happens on a tap, the page looks broken.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone who taps "Solo travellers" or "Budget" to narrow down Canggu hostels. Vibe search is one of the product's main features, so filtering is exactly what they expect these pills to do.

findings.where: Navigation: the MantaHostels logo, "Destinations" and "How we rank" in the header, the phone Menu panel, and "How we rank" in the footer
findings.fault: None of the site navigation goes anywhere. The logo, labelled "MantaHostels home", reloads this page instead of going to the home page. "Destinations" jumps to #destinations, but there is no such section on the page, so the click does nothing visible. "How we rank" reloads the same page in both the header and the footer. A visitor can't leave this guide or reach any other part of the site.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker comparing their next stop, who wants to see other Bali destinations or go back home. Also a visitor checking how hostels are ranked before trusting the guide. The ranking method is meant to be public, and here the link to it leads nowhere.

findings.where: Footer links: Privacy, Terms, Report content
findings.fault: All three links just reload this page. A visitor looking for the privacy policy or terms, or trying to report something wrong, ends up back where they started with no explanation.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor who checks the privacy policy or terms before trusting a new site. Also anyone who spots a mistake in the guide and wants to report it: the link offers a way to do that, but it doesn't work.

findings.where: The "Vibe" heading, between Surf and Good for, at both widths
findings.fault: "Vibe" is a plain heading that does nothing when tapped, but it is styled like a link: underlined, in a teal link colour, and in italics. Underline and link colour are reserved for links. The "Surf" heading at the same level is plain dark text, so the two section headings look different and "Vibe" alone looks clickable.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps "Vibe" expecting a fuller nightlife or social guide, gets nothing, and from then on is less sure which underlined text on the site is really a link.

findings.where: The "coming soon" notice above the footer, at both widths
findings.fault: This is a neutral note that listings aren't live yet, but it sits on a solid red box. Red is the colour for errors and sold-out states, so the block looks like a failure message rather than an announcement. The project's own rule puts its interior announcement on the dark ink background.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor who sees a red box at the end of the page and thinks something has failed, such as the listings not loading. That's the wrong impression on a page that is trying to earn their trust before launch.
